clue.text: Deal in some old coins

parts.note: some of a thing is a part of it
ex- is a prefix meaning former or old
loose coins are change

explanation.surface: A collector does business in antique coinage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal in' reads as trading, but 'Deal' alone is the definition and 'in' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-exchange is a trade where an old item counts towards the price of a new one, a kind of transaction.

clue.text: Chemist has gone to pull up herb

parts.note: gone means past, over

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling up a word reads it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb

explanation.surface: A pharmacist has left to uproot some plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French scientist who developed pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: He was a hero after Quebec

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic lover is the leading man of his play; in the NATO phonetic alphabet the code word for R follows the one for Q.

clue.text: "Athens ..mother of arts and "(Milton)

parts.note: the quotation from Milton's Paradise Regained, 'Athens, the eye of Greece, mother of arts and ...', is completed by the missing word

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-quotation clue: the line in Paradise Regained praises Athens as the mother of arts and of fine speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's line ends on the word for persuasive, fluent oratory, which Athens was famed for.

clue.text: Aid to cheating for lying child

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links: a cot is a bed for a child lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil's illicit notes in an exam are a crib; a baby's cot is also a crib.

clue.text: It provides support for amateur type of critic

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses: a seat with arm rests, and the armchair critic who judges from home without experience.
explanation.definitionFit: An upholstered seat holds you up; a critic without hands-on experience is described with the same word.

clue.text: Weapon bunged up, for instance, with muck

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A firearm gets clogged with dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunged up' suggests blocked, as the surface wants; here it turns EG upwards to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunge is British slang for sticky, unpleasant gunk or slime.

clue.text: Sign that the news is worrying?

definitions.text: Sign that the news is worrying?

parts.words: Sign that the news is worrying
parts.note: a worry line on the forehead is a sign of anxiety, and a big newspaper banner announces the news

explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's main banner title tells readers what is happening, while a forehead furrow shows worry.

clue.text: Caveman who made an overture

parts.note: Mendelssohn's Hebrides overture is named after a sea cave on Staffa called after a legendary hero

explanation.walkthrough: 'Caveman' suggests a prehistoric person and 'made an overture' an approach; really the hero gave his name to the Staffa cave and Mendelssohn's overture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish legendary giant has a cave on Staffa named after him, celebrated in Mendelssohn's concert overture.

clue.text: Party conference

explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece a symposium was a drinking party; today it is an academic meeting where papers are discussed.

clue.text: Skin blemishes when a vein ruptures

indicators.note: a vein that ruptures bursts apart, so its letters with the a are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Marks appear on the skin when a blood vessel bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi are birthmarks or moles, the plural of naevus, coloured patches on the skin.

clue.text: Issue a book

explanation.definitionFit: An issue can mean a going out or departure, as in a mass flight of people; the second book of the Old Testament bears the same name.

clue.text: Animal finds tail such a trial, maybe

parts.note: a sheep is a farm animal
to tail someone is to follow them closely, to dog them

explanation.surface: A creature finds its tail a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning follow. The definition works as an adjective: a sheepdog trial is a herding competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Herding contests for collies are called trials, so the compound describes that kind of competition.

clue.text: Appear mad, hiding in such dangerous terrain

indicators.note: the word rave hides the word in, holding it inside itself

parts.note: to rave is to talk wildly, as if out of one's mind

explanation.surface: Someone acting crazily takes cover in rough, perilous country.
explanation.definitionFit: A ravine is a deep narrow gorge, steep and risky ground to cross.

clue.text: Such fine glasses, but could be blind

explanation.walkthrough: 'but' links the two senses: Murano glassware and a slatted window blind.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine glassware from Murano and a slatted window shade both take the name of the Italian city.

clue.text: Gluttons desire for food, though unfit for humans

parts.note: greedy eaters are called pigs
will can mean wish or desire

explanation.surface: Greedy eaters long for something to eat, even if it's not fit for people.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has 'Gluttons'' with an apostrophe, dropped in the OCR.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is kitchen waste fed to swine, edible only for livestock.

clue.text: Minor things — not even pint-sized

explanation.definitionFit: Trivial matters are called small beer; jokingly, a weak little ale is too slight to fill a pint.

clue.text: To lie in the sun in tropical Africa brings day of reckoning

indicators.note: in places the sunbathing word inside the African country

parts.note: the Congo is a region of equatorial Africa
to tan is to sunbathe until brown

explanation.surface: Sunbathing in equatorial Africa leads to a reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Contango is an old London Stock Exchange term: contango day was when deferred bargains were settled.
explanation.definitionFit: On the old Stock Exchange, settlement terms for carrying over bargains were fixed on a particular date, the time of accounting.

clue.text: Knight took chance on weapon

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: a lance is a long spear used by mounted knights
a lot is something decided by chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: A knight risked all on his weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took' is only a link word; 'chance on weapon' puts LOT after LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the most famous of King Arthur's Round Table champions.

clue.text: Heard to progress awkwardly with this rear puncture

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for clumsy movement is said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and clumsily

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles along awkwardly after an injection in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links. A lumbar puncture draws fluid from the lower spine.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinal tap taken from the lower back is called by this adjective, relating to the loins.

clue.text: Press for identification

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses: identity documents are papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The press means newspapers collectively; documents proving who you are are also called by that name.

clue.text: Justice is called for in court

explanation.definitionFit: Justice Silence is a country magistrate in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 2; 'Silence in court!' is the usher's call for quiet.

clue.text: US college has single entry to make things easier

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
I is the Roman numeral one
a gate is a way in

explanation.surface: An American university admits one student to smooth the way.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to lessen the severity of something, easing a situation.

clue.text: Spirit that rubber may produce

parts.note: rubber means one who rubs, like Aladdin polishing his lamp to summon its spirit

explanation.definitionFit: Aladdin rubbed his lamp and out came the magical jinn of the Arabian Nights.

clue.text: Sort of clock that does best on summer time?

definitions.text: Sort of clock that does best on summer time?

parts.words: Sort of clock that does best on summer time
parts.note: a clock planted in a park flowerbed looks best in summer when the blooms are out, a joke on clocks and summer time

explanation.definitionFit: Parks lay out clock faces in beds of flowers, so the clock is described by the adjective for blossoms.

clue.text: Sway — we hear it falls

indicators.note: we hear signals the word for falling water is spoken to give a different spelling

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Something sways as it tumbles down, we're told.
explanation.definitionFit: Sway is power or rule, as a monarch holds over a kingdom.

clue.text: In horse-race, back this Olympic champion

indicators.note: back means those letters are read from right to left
in tells us the letters sit inside the words horse-race

explanation.surface: A gold medallist rides in a horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like betting on a horse; here it turns the run SERA, inside horse-race, into the god.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of war was one of the twelve gods of Olympus, a mighty warrior.

clue.text: A new union making a profit

indicators.note: union signals the joining together of the pieces side by side

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A newly formed trade union is doing well financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A new' read as one word, 'anew', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means once more, a fresh repetition.

clue.text: Quisling was wearing no combinations

indicators.note: combinations of letters means the letters of wearing no are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: The traitor went without his long underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Combinations are also an old one-piece undergarment, which gives the comic surface. Vidkun Quisling led Norway's wartime collaborationist government.
explanation.definitionFit: Vidkun Quisling was a native of Norway, collaborating with the Nazi occupiers.

clue.text: Complaint about abnormal mental state after battle

indicators.note: after places the trance piece behind the battle piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Mons in Belgium was the site of a famous 1914 battle
a trance is a dazed, hypnotic state

explanation.surface: A grievance about an odd frame of mind following combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a forceful protest or objection.
